Home Business Lifestyle Tutorials Technology Politics Education Sports Public Info Automotive Opinion Economy Health Home Business Boeing Workers Face Strike Vote as Contract Expiration Nears Boeing Workers Face Strike Vote as Contract Expiration Nears Sarah Mitchell Published Oct 2, 2026 - 03:11 3 Reads Last Update Oct 2, 2026 - 03:11 Share WhatsApp EXTREME-PHOTOGRAPHER / Getty Images Smallest Font Largest Font Boeing offered a 32 percent wage increase to roughly 17,000 engineers and technical workers ahead of an October 6 contract expiration, setting up a potential strike as early as October 7 if union members reject the proposal. The labor dispute follows a multi-month strike by Boeing workers in 2025 as the company attempts to reach an agreement with its largest white-collar union. Advertisement Scroll To Continue with Content For early retirees participating in a potential walkout, union strike benefits trigger distinct regulatory treatments between federal tax obligations and Social Security calculations. While the Internal Revenue Service classifies strike and lockout payments as taxable income under IRS Publication 525, Social Security considers ordinary strike benefits as non-wage income. Also Read Social Security Sends 90 Dollar Medicare Rebate This tax distinction prevents ordinary strike benefits from counting toward the Social Security retirement earnings test, which otherwise reduces benefit payments for early retirees who earn above annual limits before reaching full retirement age. Under current rules, ordinary strike benefits avoid earnings-test limits regardless of whether workers perform picket duties or remain on call. However, separate union payments designated specifically for strike duties count as reportable wages once they equal or exceed $100 within a calendar year.
